title: cbuild_settings
description: A kit's settings from 1.2.0 on, stored in the _cbuild_settings product meta (D-354). A kit with none, or a setting left out, has the default. A setting this release does not know is let through, so a later release can add one here and a rollback to this one still reads the kit. A new kit setting goes here, never as a new key in an older document.

schema_version.description: The document's version. Version 1 is the only one so far.

builder_page.description: The page the kit's builder is on, by its ID: a published page that holds the kit's Builder block, chosen in the Build tab. Left out, the kit's own page. A page that is no longer published, or no longer holds the block, is not used, and the kit's own page is.

lead_days.description: How many business days putting a build together takes, from 1.2.0 (#142): a count, such as 2, or a range, the fewer first, such as 2-4, from 0 to 60. Shown beside the lead time in the Build tab's Assembly section, and given to cbuild_arrival_estimate and cbuild_delivery_line for an assembled build. Left out, none.

guide.description: Whether the builder offers "Help me choose", the guided start's questions, at its start, from 1.3.0 (D-409). Off, the page draws no disclosure, form or builds, and answers in a link recommend nothing. The default is true.

picks.description: Whether a card in the builder says which ready builds pick its part, such as "Picked for Street", from 1.3.0 (#137, D-409). Off, no card says it. The default is true.

ratings.description: Whether a card in the builder shows its part's rating, a star and its score, from 1.3.0 (#137, D-409). Off, no card shows them; on, none show while WooCommerce's star ratings are off. The default is true.

start_button.description: Whether the kit places "Build a complete with this deck" on the pages of the parts its first slot offers. Off, the kit is passed over, and another kit that offers the part may place it. The default is true.

swaps.description: Whether the builder offers smart swaps, from 1.3.0 (#135): on the review and on the picked card, a part for less and a better one that fit the build. Off, the state route's answer has none and the builder shows no swap control. The default is true.

tricks.description: Whether the 3D view offers its trick buttons, from 1.4.0 (#139, D-474): ollie, kickflip, heelflip, pop shove-it and 360 flip. It matters only where view_3d is on, and the Build tab shows it only then. The default is true.

view_3d.description: Whether the builder offers "View in 3D", from 1.4.0 (#139, D-474): a 3D view of the build drawn from its parts' sizes, loaded only when pressed. Off, the page draws no 3D button and the builder's view has no scene. Left out, as in every kit saved before 1.4.0, it is false, so an update changes no builder; a new kit's first Build tab save stores it true (D-476).

width_guide.description: "Not sure of your width?" under the deck step's width question. Left out, the guide is shown with the plugin's rows, by US shoe size.

shown.description: Whether the guide is on the page. Off, it is left out of the page and of the state route's answer, and its rows are kept. The default is true.

rows.description: The shop's own rows, in the order shown. Left out, the guide has the plugin's rows, in the shopper's language.

shoe.description: The shoe size, as the shop writes it: EU 40 to 42. Plain text.

from.description: The narrowest deck it rides, in inches, from 5 to 12, with a point and up to four decimals.

to.description: The widest, in inches, no narrower than from. Left out or empty, the row says from and wider.

wheel_guide.description: From 1.3.0 (#134): the wheel sizes the guided start recommends for each riding style, in millimetres. Left out, or a style with no row, the plugin's sizes, from published wheel guides: street 50 to 54, park 53 to 56, bowl 55 to 58 and cruising 59 to 65.

rows.description: The shop's own sizes, a row a riding style at most.

style.description: The riding style the guided start asks about.

from.description: The smallest wheel it recommends, in millimetres, from 40 to 90, with a point and up to four decimals.

to.description: The largest, in millimetres, no smaller than from. Left out or empty, from alone.
